newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan urges Iraqi withdrawal from Kurd areas.
newsitem.headline: Japan urges Iraqi withdrawal from Kurd areas.

text.p: Japan on Wednesday called on Iraq to immediately withdraw its forces from Kurdish areas of the country to end what Tokyo's ambassador to the United Nations said was a clear violation of relevant U.N. resolutions.

United Nations ambassador Hisashi Owada told a news conference in Tokyo there was no doubt Baghdad was in breach of 1991 U.N. resolutions calling on the Iraqi government to end the persecution of ethnic and religious minorities, including the Kurds in northern Iraq.

"Iraq has clearly violated the relevant U.N. resolutions," said Owada, who declined to comment on the United States' two sets of air raids on targets in southern Iraq. Earlier, deputy government spokesman Kazo Watanabe said the crisis could be settled only by an Iraqi withdrawal.

"Japan strongly hopes for Iraq to withdraw from the northern areas (of Iraq) in order to settle the situation at the earliest possible instant," Watanabe, speaking minutes after the United States announced its second missile attack on Iraq, told a news conference.

Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto reiterated a statement he made on Tuesday that "Japan understands and supports the actions taken by the United States' military forces, as long as they are necessary to ensure Iraqi compliance with relevant U.N. Security Council Resolutions."
Hashimoto told reporters he was concerned at the size of forces Iraq was moving into Kurdish areas.

"Although I haven't actually seen everything on a satellite or anything, I am concerned that the Iraqis are moving thousands of military men and hundreds of tanks to the Kurdish area," Hashimoto said.
